'''Wolfgang Viechtbauer''' is a statistician. He is an associate professor of methodology and statistics at the [[Maastricht University]] in the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences and Faculty of Psychology and Neuroscience. His most influential work has been focused on the field of [[meta-analysis]] and evidence synthesis.

== Education ==
Viechtbauer completed a M.A. (2002) and a Ph.D. (2004) at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite thesis|title=Bias of certain variance estimators in meta-analysis|date=2002|language=en|first=Wolfgang|last=Viechtbauer|oclc=52367230}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite thesis|title=Choosing between the fixed-, random-, and mixed-effects model in meta-analysis: an analysis of existing and new model selection methods|date=2004|language=en|first=Wolfgang|last=Viechtbauer|oclc=61135330|isbn=978-0-496-14066-4}}</ref> His master's thesis was titled ''Bias of certain variance estimators in meta-analysis'' and his dissertation was titled ''Choosing between the fixed-, random-, and mixed-effects model in meta-analysis: an analysis of existing and new model selection methods''.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> His doctoral advisor was [[David Budescu]].<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
Viechtbauer is an [[associate professor]] of methodology and statistics at the [[Maastricht University]] in the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences and Faculty of Psychology and [[Neuroscience]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=W. Viechtbauer - |url=https://www.maastrichtuniversity.nl/wolfgang.viechtbauer |access-date=22 April 2020 |website=Maastricht University}}</ref>

==Research and software==
Viechtbauer’s research centres on statistical methods for meta-analysis, including heterogeneity estimation, publication-bias diagnostics and multilevel or multivariate models.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Viechtbauer |first1=Wolfgang |last2=Cheung |first2=Mike W.-L. |date=2010 |title=Outlier and influence diagnostics for meta-analysis |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jrsm.11 |journal=Research Synthesis Methods |language=en |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=112–125 |doi=10.1002/jrsm.11|pmid=26061377 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 2009 he released metafor, an [[R package]] that provides a comprehensive suite of functions for computing effect sizes, fitting fixed-, random- and mixed-effects models, and producing diagnostic graphics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Viechtbauer |first=Wolfgang |date=2010 |title=Conducting Meta-Analyses in R with the metafor Package |url=http://www.jstatsoft.org/v36/i03/ |journal=Journal of Statistical Software |language=en |volume=36 |issue=3 |doi=10.18637/jss.v036.i03 |doi-access=free |issn=1548-7660}}</ref> The JSS article introducing metafor has received more than 18,000 citations in Google Scholar as of May 2025,<ref>{{citation|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=J89RXJkAAAAJ|title=Google Scholar profile: Wolfgang Viechtbauer|access-date=25 May 2025}}</ref> and the software is referenced in methodological tutorials, and domain-specific guides across health, ecology, education and psychology.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Haddaway |first1=Neal |last2=Grainger |first2=Matthew |date=2019-03-15 |title=Building metafor |url=https://www.eshackathon.org/2019/03/15/building-metafor.html |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=Evidence Synthesis Hackathon |language=en}}</ref>
